articles.title: Inside the sensor shortage that delayed three camera launches this year
articles.subtitle: A component nobody outside the industry usually thinks about
articles.excerpt: A shortage of a single sensor component pushed back launch dates across three major camera lines this year.
articles.author: ashraf

content.text: Three separate camera launches slipped their announced release windows this year, and all three manufacturers eventually pointed to the same root cause: a shortage of a specific sensor-stacking component sourced from a small number of suppliers.
Why one part can stall a whole product line
Unlike more commoditized components, high-end stacked sensors have very few qualified suppliers, so a disruption at one factory can ripple across multiple brands at once.
Manufacturers say supply is stabilizing, with delayed models now expected within the next two quarters.

articles.title: The megapixel race quietly ended. Here's what replaced it
articles.subtitle: Camera marketing stopped leading with a number a few years ago
articles.excerpt: Camera spec sheets used to open with a megapixel count. Now the number that gets top billing is something else entirely.
articles.author: admin

content.text: There was a stretch of years where every camera launch led with a bigger megapixel count than the last. That race has quietly wound down, and manufacturers now lead with computational processing and sensor size instead.
What actually changed
Most casual buyers hit diminishing returns on resolution well before professionals did, and manufacturers noticed that marketing around low-light performance and video capability converted better.

items: Sensor size now gets top billing over resolution
Computational processing is marketed as a headline feature
Video specs increasingly outrank stills specs in launch materials

articles.title: Why film cameras are suddenly back on store shelves
articles.subtitle: A format the industry left for dead is getting new stock again
articles.excerpt: After years of discontinued lines and secondhand-only availability, several manufacturers are putting new film cameras back into production.
articles.author: ashraf

content.text: For most of the last two decades, buying a new film camera meant buying secondhand. That's starting to change as demand from a younger, largely first-time film audience has convinced a few manufacturers it's worth restarting limited production.
Who's actually buying these
Retailers report the bulk of buyers are under 30 and have never owned a film camera before, treating it more as a deliberate creative choice than a nostalgia purchase.
Film stock pricing remains the biggest barrier to sustained growth in the category, with some popular stocks still selling out within days of restocking.

articles.title: How action cameras learned to shoot in near total darkness
articles.subtitle: Sensor tech trickles down from professional gear
articles.excerpt: Low-light performance used to be the exclusive domain of expensive mirrorless bodies. That's changing fast for rugged action cameras.
articles.author: admin

content.text: Overview
Low-light performance used to be the exclusive domain of expensive mirrorless bodies. That's changing fast for rugged action cameras.
Sensor tech trickles down

Sensor tech trickles down from professional gear. Low-light performance used to be the exclusive domain of expensive mirrorless bodies, but the sensor size in this generation of action cameras has grown by 25% compared to three years ago, and that extra surface area is doing most of the work.

In our test footage, shot at dusk with no supplemental lighting, noise stayed manageable down to roughly 3 lux, a threshold that would have been unusable on this category of camera as recently as two generations ago.
Stabilization in the dark

Image stabilization gets noticeably more aggressive in low light to compensate for longer exposure times, and the crop that results is more visible than in daylight — worth knowing if you're framing tight shots.

Battery drain is the other tradeoff: continuous night recording pulled through a full charge in just under 70 minutes in our testing, roughly 20 minutes shorter than the same camera shooting in daylight.
Our take
It's an encouraging sign for where the category is headed next, even if not every question has been answered yet — battery life in cold, dark conditions is still the biggest limiting factor.
